blocks.content:
Judicial Review is the power of the Supreme Court to examine laws and declare them unconstitutional if they violate the Constitution.

It protects the supremacy of the Constitution.
It protects the supremacy of the Constitution.

items: Judicial Review empowers the Supreme Court, not lower bodies, to examine the constitutionality of laws.
The ground for declaring any law unconstitutional is its violation of the Constitution.
The core constitutional objective of Judicial Review is protecting constitutional supremacy.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Judicial Review is the specific power granted to the Supreme Court to examine legislation.
Laws are declared unconstitutional if they are found to violate the Constitution.
The primary function of Judicial Review is to protect and uphold the supremacy of the Constitution.
